title: Modification of fast-slow differential agar medium for selective isolation of lactic acid bacteria
author: Güley, Fallico, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Component A solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 19 g sodium glycerophosphate (catalog G5422, Sigma‑Aldrich), 2.5 g yeast extract (catalog LP0021, Oxoid), 0.5 g L‑ascorbic acid (catalog A7506, Sigma‑Aldrich) and 10 g agar in 550 mL distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare Component B solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 g skim milk powder (catalog LP0031, Oxoid) in 450 mL distilled water.

steps.title: Autoclave Component A
steps.instruction: Sterilize Component A by autoclaving at 121 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Autoclave Component B
steps.instruction: Sterilize Component B by autoclaving at 121 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Cool components to 55 °C
steps.instruction: Place the sterilized Component A and Component B in a water bath and cool each to 55 °C.

steps.title: Combine components A and B
steps.instruction: Mix the cooled Component A and Component B together by gentle swirling.

steps.title: Add antibiotics and indicator
steps.instruction: Add nalidixic acid sodium salt to a final concentration of 40 µg mL⁻¹ and bromocresol purple to 0.004 % (w/v) while the medium is at 55 °C, then mix gently.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a nalidixic acid sodium salt solution at 40 µg mL⁻¹ (use the sodium salt; the salt‑free form is insoluble) and filter‑sterilize it before use.
Add the filter‑sterilized nalidixic acid solution to the cooled medium.
Add bromocresol purple (catalog 1.03025, Merck) to achieve 0.004 % (w/v).

steps.title: Pour medium into petri dishes
steps.instruction: Dispense the finished mFSDA agar into sterile petri dishes and allow to solidify.
